title: Story 01: New Feature Request — Full Lifecycle
pmResponse:
# Testing Mode — Written Plan Only

I'm in testing mode, so I will not execute any commands or tools (including the `npm run expert-manager` hook). Below is the complete, ordered action plan I would follow as Project Manager for this feature lifecycle. I've assumed issue IDs `#1`–`#8` are assigned in creation order; in a real run I would read each ID from the `create` output and substitute it into subsequent commands.

---

## Phase 0 — Orient & Verify

### Action 0.1 — Confirm the work queue is empty and no duplicate exists
```
agt list
agt list --tags feature
```
**Reasoning:** The scenario says the queue is empty, but I always verify before creating issues. `agt list` confirms nothing is in progress, and a tag-filtered search ensures this feature isn't already tracked. This prevents duplicate parent issues.

---

## Phase 1 — Create the Parent Initiative

### Action 1.1 — Create the parent feature issue
```
agt create "Add search functionality to the issue list" \
  --description "Add the ability to search and filter the issue list so users can quickly find issues by free text, status, tags, or assignee. Covers the full feature lifecycle: architecture spec → library implementation → webapp UI → validation/testing → release." \
  --tags initiative,feature \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --priority 3
```
**Reasoning:** This is the umbrella issue I own as PM. It tracks the whole feature. I leave it in `todo` for now — I'll flip it to `in-progress` only after the full breakdown + sync tracker are in place (Step 4), which is what stops the work loop from re-waking me each cycle. Tag `initiative,feature` marks it as the top-level coordinating issue.

→ Assume this returns **#1**.

---

## Phase 2 — Break Down into Phase Child Issues (Plan → Dev → Validate → Release)

All children get `--parentId #1` and start in `todo`. Only the first (Planning) is immediately actionable; the rest are gated by blockages I add in Step 3.

### Action 2.1 — Planning child (Library architect)
```
agt create "Design search functionality architecture and API spec" \
  --description "Design the architecture and API for issue-list search. Define supported parameters (free-text, status, tags, assignee), the CLI flags for `agt list`, and the contract the webapp will consume. Deliverable: a spec that unblocks both library and webapp development." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee library-architect \
  --status todo \
  --parentId #1
```
**Reasoning:** Features flow Plan → Dev → Validate → Release. `library-architect` owns the planning phase. This is the only unblocked child, so work begins here immediately.
→ Assume **#2**.

### Action 2.2 — Development child (Library developer)
```
agt create "Implement search filtering in the agt list command" \
  --description "Implement search/filtering in the `agt list` command per the architecture spec. Support text search and structured filters (status, tags, assignee). Expose search capability for the webapp to consume." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee library-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId #1
```
**Reasoning:** Library implementation of the search. Blocked until the spec (#2) lands. Assigned to `library-developer` (development phase).
→ Assume **#3**.

### Action 2.3 — Development child (Webapp developer)
```
agt create "Implement search UI in webapp issue list view" \
  --description "Implement a search UI in the webapp issue list view, integrating with the library search API as defined in the spec. Add a search input, filter controls, and result rendering. Coordinate with the spec for the API contract." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee webapp-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId #1
```
**Reasoning:** The webapp side of the feature. The `webapp-developer` handles planning + development, so they'll read the spec and build the UI. This runs in parallel with #3 once planning is done. Blocked by the spec (#2).
→ Assume **#4**.

### Action 2.4 — Validation child (Library validator)
```
agt create "Write and run tests for search in the library" \
  --description "Write unit/integration tests for the search functionality in the library. Verify text search, status/tag/assignee filters, and edge cases. Reproduce and file any bugs found." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee library-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId #1
```
**Reasoning:** Library validation phase. Can't test until the library implementation (#3) exists. Assigned to `library-validator`.
→ Assume **#5**.

### Action 2.5 — Validation child (Webapp validator)
```
agt create "Write E2E tests for search in the webapp" \
  --description "Write E2E tests for the search UI in the webapp. Verify search input, filter controls, and result rendering. Reproduce and file any visual/functional bugs." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee webapp-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId #1
```
**Reasoning:** Webapp validation phase. Blocked until the webapp implementation (#4) exists. Assigned to `webapp-validator`.
→ Assume **#6**.

### Action 2.6 — Release child (Library releaser)
```
agt create "Release search functionality" \
  --description "Run the full test suite, generate docs, build, and publish the search functionality. Confirm both library (#5) and webapp (#6) validations pass before releasing." \
  --tags task,feature \
  --assignee library-releaser \
  --status todo \
  --parentId #1
```
**Reasoning:** Release is the final worker phase. The team has a single releaser (`library-releaser`), so it owns the consolidated release. Blocked by both validations to guarantee nothing ships untested.
→ Assume **#7**.

### Action 2.7 — Sync tracker child (PM-owned)
```
agt create "Sync: Search functionality complete" \
  --description "Sync tracker for the search functionality feature. Fires when the release (#7) completes. Used by the PM to confirm the lifecycle is finished, close out the parent, and report results to stakeholders." \
  --tags sync \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId #1
```
**Reasoning:** This is the signal-back mechanism. It's assigned to me and blocked by the last worker child (release #7). When it unblocks, the work loop wakes me to verify, close the parent, and report. Until then I stay out of the way and workers drive all transitions.
→ Assume **#8**.

---

## Phase 3 — Wire Up the Blockages (Dependency Chain)

Format: `agt blockages add <blockedId> --by <blockerId> [...]`

### Action 3.1 — Development blocked by Planning
```
agt blockages add #3 --by #2
agt blockages add #4 --by #2
```
**Reasoning:** Both dev streams (library #3, webapp #4) must wait for the architecture spec (#2). This enforces Plan → Dev.

### Action 3.2 — Validation blocked by Development
```
agt blockages add #5 --by #3
agt blockages add #6 --by #4
```
**Reasoning:** Each validation can only start once its corresponding implementation lands (library test ← library code; webapp test ← webapp code). This enforces Dev → Validate per sub-team.

### Action 3.3 — Release blocked by both Validations
```
agt blockages add #7 --by #5 #6
```
**Reasoning:** Release must not ship until both the library and webapp have passed validation. A single release consolidates the two streams. This enforces Validate → Release.

### Action 3.4 — Sync tracker blocked by Release
```
agt blockages add #8 --by #7
```
**Reasoning:** The sync tracker fires only after release completes — the definitive "feature is done" signal that wakes me as PM.

---

## Phase 4 — Activate the Feature & Document the Plan

### Action 4.1 — Set the parent to in-progress
```
agt update #1 --status in-progress
```
**Reasoning:** Per the trigger, flipping the parent to `in-progress` prevents the work loop from re-waking me every cycle. I've finished all setup; from here the worker agents drive child transitions. I only wake when the sync tracker (#8) unblocks.

### Action 4.2 — Record the breakdown as a comment on the parent
```
agt comments add #1 --content "Feature lifecycle set up for 'Add search functionality to the issue list'. Breakdown by phase (Plan → Dev → Validate → Release):

- #2 [Plan] library-architect — architecture & API spec (unblocked, work starts here)
- #3 [Dev/Lib] library-developer — blocked by #2
- #4 [Dev/Web] webapp-developer — blocked by #2
- #5 [Validate/Lib] library-validator — blocked by #3
- #6 [Validate/Web] webapp-validator — blocked by #4
- #7 [Release] library-releaser — blocked by #5 and #6
- #8 [Sync] project-manager — blocked by #7 (wake PM to close out)

Parent set to in-progress. Worker agents own the child transitions from here; PM waits for the sync tracker to fire."
```
**Reasoning:** Documents the plan, dependencies, and ownership for anyone (or any agent) inspecting the issue. Captures the rationale and the handoff so the state is self-explanatory.

---

## Phase 5 — (Later) When the Sync Tracker Fires — Close-Out Plan

I do **not** run these now. I list them so the full lifecycle is explicit. When #8 unblocks (release done), I would:

```
agt update #8 --status in-progress
agt comments add #1 --content "Feature complete. All phases passed: plan, library + webapp dev, library + webapp validation, and release. Closing out."
agt update #1 --status done
agt update #8 --status done
```
**Reasoning:** Verify the release landed, post a success summary on the parent (PM-facing detail, skipping irrelevant internals), mark the parent `done`, and close the sync tracker. If any blocker had surfaced during the lifecycle (e.g., a validation found a bug), the responsible agent would have created a `bug` issue, re-routed via the project-manager, and I would have adjusted the chain — e.g., inserting `agt blockages add <release> --by <bug-fix>` until resolved.

---

## Final Issue Hierarchy

```
#1  "Add search functionality to the issue list"   [initiative,feature]  assignee: project-manager  status: in-progress
 │
 ├── #2  "Design search functionality architecture and API spec"   [task,feature]  library-architect  todo   ← STARTS HERE (unblocked)
 │
 ├── #3  "Implement search filtering in the agt list command"      [task,feature]  library-developer  todo   ⛔ blocked by #2
 │
 ├── #4  "Implement search UI in webapp issue list view"           [task,feature]  webapp-developer   todo   ⛔ blocked by #2
 │
 ├── #5  "Write and run tests for search in the library"           [task,feature]  library-validator  todo   ⛔ blocked by #3
 │
 ├── #6  "Write E2E tests for search in the webapp"                [task,feature]  webapp-validator   todo   ⛔ blocked by #4
 │
 ├── #7  "Release search functionality"                            [task,feature]  library-releaser   todo   ⛔ blocked by #5, #6
 │
 └── #8  "Sync: Search functionality complete"                     [sync]          project-manager    todo   ⛔ blocked by #7  (wakes PM)
```

**Dependency / phase flow:**

```
#2 Plan ─┬─► #3 Lib Dev ─► #5 Lib Validate ─┐
         │                                   ├─► #7 Release ─► #8 Sync (PM)
         └─► #4 Web Dev ─► #6 Web Validate ──┘
```

---

## Summary of Commands (in execution order)

| # | Command | Purpose |
|---|---------|---------|
| 0.1 | `agt list` / `agt list --tags feature` | Verify empty queue, no dup |
| 1.1 | `agt create "Add search functionality…" …` (#1) | Parent initiative |
| 2.1 | `agt create "Design search…" --parentId #1` (#2) | Planning → architect |
| 2.2 | `agt create "Implement search filtering…" --parentId #1` (#3) | Lib dev |
| 2.3 | `agt create "Implement search UI…" --parentId #1` (#4) | Web dev |
| 2.4 | `agt create "Write and run tests… library" --parentId #1` (#5) | Lib validate |
| 2.5 | `agt create "Write E2E tests… webapp" --parentId #1` (#6) | Web validate |
| 2.6 | `agt create "Release search…" --parentId #1` (#7) | Release |
| 2.7 | `agt create "Sync: Search… complete" --parentId #1` (#8) | Sync tracker (PM) |
| 3.1 | `agt blockages add #3 --by #2` / `#4 --by #2` | Plan gates Dev |
| 3.2 | `agt blockages add #5 --by #3` / `#6 --by #4` | Dev gates Validate |
| 3.3 | `agt blockages add #7 --by #5 #6` | Validate gates Release |
| 3.4 | `agt blockages add #8 --by #7` | Release gates Sync |
| 4.1 | `agt update #1 --status in-progress` | Activate; stop PM wake cycles |
| 4.2 | `agt comments add #1 --content "…"` | Document breakdown |

---

## Notes & Open Considerations

- **No webapp release step:** The team has only a `library-releaser`. The consolidated release (#7) bundles both sub-teams' work. If webapp deployment is ever needed separately, that would be a new `chore`/`task` issue to raise with the project-manager.
- **Planning scope:** I used a single planning issue (library-architect) whose spec feeds both dev streams. The webapp-developer's built-in planning role is satisfied by consuming that spec rather than a duplicate planning ticket — avoids over-decomposition.
- **Bug handling during lifecycle:** If validation surfaces a bug, the validator creates a `bug` issue, and I'd add it as a blocker to the affected downstream phase (e.g., block release by the fix) until resolved — standard re-routing without disturbing the rest of the chain.
- **Testing-mode caveat:** I did not run the `npm run expert-manager` hook or any tooling per the testing-mode restriction. In a live run I'd execute the commands above sequentially, reading each returned ID before referencing it.
feedback: Strong response with excellent adherence to the sync tracker pattern (child assigned to PM, blocked by last worker child), correct parent todo→in-progress transition after children are created, and sound dependency wiring. The phase-to-agent mapping is correct for all library phases (planning→architect, dev→developer, validate→validator, release→releaser, sync→PM). However, the agent expanded scope beyond the expected linear 4-task library pipeline by adding webapp-developer and webapp-validator tasks, creating an 8-issue DAG instead of the expected 5-issue linear chain. Minor tag deviations: parent tagged initiative,feature instead of feature; children tagged task,feature instead of task; sync tracker tagged sync instead of task,sync. Core key behaviors and all expected actions are fully covered.
